# @neural-ng/editor

Import canonical `NeuralEditor` from `@neural-ng/editor`. `EditorComponent` is
a deprecated compatibility alias. The selector remains `<neural-editor>`.

## Public API boundary

- Treat `API_FREEZE.md` as the authoritative standalone package contract.
- Import only from `@neural-ng/editor`. Never deep-import source files.
- Use `NeuralEditor`, the exported template directives, public types,
  constants, serializers, pure helpers, and `NeuralEditorController`.
- Internal toolbar, menu, review, and collaboration-panel renderer components
  are not public API. Customize through class slots and template directives.
- Do not use raw Tiptap/ProseMirror operation or tracked-change helpers. Use the
  controller methods so revisions, events, forms, and collaboration rules stay
  consistent.

## Canonical rules

- Install only `@neural-ng/editor`. Tiptap, ProseMirror, Floating UI, Yjs, and the required NeuralNg core runtime are package-managed dependencies.
- Install a realtime collaboration transport/provider separately only when collaboration is enabled.
- Import `NeuralEditor` from `@neural-ng/editor`.
- Bind only `NeuralEditorDocument` JSON to `[(value)]`, `[formField]`,
  `[formControl]`, or `[(ngModel)]`. Never bind HTML or Markdown strings and
  never create a string-or-JSON value union.
- The empty value is a `doc` containing an empty paragraph. Do not use `null` as
  the normal empty state.
- Treat editor values as immutable. Do not mutate node, mark, attribute, or
  content arrays in place.

## Beta schema, identity, menus, AI review, and collaboration

- Text alignment is stored on paragraph or heading attributes as `textAlign`.
- Text color is stored in a `textStyle` mark with a `color` attribute.
- Highlight is stored in a `highlight` mark and may include a `color` attribute.
- Tasks use `taskList` and `taskItem`; task state is the boolean `checked`
  attribute on `taskItem`.
- Tables use `table`, `tableRow`, `tableHeader`, and `tableCell` nodes.
- Images use an `image` node. Persist a stable HTTP(S) URL and optional alt,
  title, width, and height attributes. Never persist File objects, blob URLs,
  or temporary object URLs.
- Mentions use `mention` nodes with stable `id` and `label` attributes. Provider-only
  metadata is not persisted. Do not copy avatars, permissions, or mutable profile
  objects into editor JSON.
- Do not invent HTML-only state that cannot be represented by the configured
  JSON schema.

## Commands

- Use the `NeuralEditorController` from `editorReady` for all programmatic
  edits. Do not query, replace, or mutate the `contenteditable` DOM.
- Use `setTextAlign()`, `setTextColor()`, `setHighlight()`,
  `toggleTaskList()`, `insertTable()`, `insertImage()`, and menu controller
  methods for Alpha 2.3 features.
- Table row, column, merge, split, header, and delete commands are contextual;
  call `controller.can(command)` before presenting a custom enabled action.
- Use `toolbarItems` for the built-in toolbar or project
  `ng-template[neuralEditorToolbar]` with `let-editor` for a custom toolbar.
- Built-in color and table menus use NeuralNg Popover in the browser top layer. Do not replace them with native `details`, custom absolute-positioned panels, or `appendTo="body"` logic. Only one auto popover remains open at a time.
- Use `(imageInsertRequest)` to open FileUpload or an application media picker.
  Upload outside Editor, then call `event.controller.insertImage()` with the
  persistent URL. Editor must not send HTTP requests.
- BubbleMenu appears for a text or image selection. FloatingMenu appears for an
  empty paragraph. Link editing uses the same contextual bubble layer so only
  one contextual menu is active.
- Context menus append to `body` by default. Use `menuAppendTo="editor"` or a
  concrete HTMLElement only when the containing stacking context is required.
- Customize menus with `neuralEditorBubbleMenu`, `neuralEditorFloatingMenu`,
  and `neuralEditorLinkPopover` templates. Use the supplied controller and link
  context callbacks; do not access the raw Tiptap instance or position menus
  manually.
- `textColors` and `highlightColors` configure UI palettes only. They do not
  constrain externally loaded JSON; validate allowed values in application and
  server code when a restricted palette is required.

## Node identity and structured operations

- Node IDs are enabled by default. Canonical JSON stores the configured
  `nodeIdAttribute` (`neuralId` by default) on identified nodes.
- Keep node IDs stable and unique. Do not derive IDs from array indexes,
  document positions, visible text, or mutable labels.
- Use `identifiedNodeTypes` and `nodeIdGenerator` only as initialization-time
  configuration. Disable `enableNodeIds` only when no operation, AI review,
  comment, or collaboration layer will address nodes.
- Prefer `controller.getNodeById()` and `controller.getNodeIdAt()` over walking
  the `contenteditable` DOM or assuming ProseMirror positions remain stable.
- Create batches with `controller.createOperationBatch()`. It captures the
  current document-only revision. Validate with `validateOperations()` and
  apply with `applyOperations()`.
- Supported operation types are `insert`, `replace`, `delete`, and
  `update-node`. Prefer `{ nodeId }` targets. Use `{ from, to }` only for a
  captured selection range from the same base revision.
- Operation batches are atomic. Never apply operations one by one in
  application code. One invalid target, node, attribute, or schema placement
  rejects the whole batch without partial changes.
- Treat `status: 'conflict'` as a required rebase/retry boundary. Never force a
  stale batch onto a newer document or silently replace its `baseRevision`.
- Inserted operation content cannot choose internal node IDs. Compatible
  single-node replacements preserve the target ID by default. The protected ID
  attribute cannot be changed with `update-node`.
- Listen to `operationsApplied`, `operationsRejected`, and `operationConflict`
  for application side effects. The form model changes only after a successful
  atomic dispatch.
- `editorDocumentToHtml()` omits node IDs by default. Use
  `{ includeNodeIds: true }` only for diagnostics or explicit round trips.
  Persist canonical JSON, not generated HTML, as the addressable source.
- Use `editorDocumentWithNodeIds()` to migrate legacy JSON before storing or
  sending it to an AI operation service.

## Slash, mention, and command-palette behavior

- Type `/` in a paragraph for the slash menu. Configure static commands through
  `slashCommands` or use `slashCommandProvider`; a provider replaces default
  filtering for that request.
- Enable mentions with `mentionProvider`. It may return synchronously or
  asynchronously. Honor the provider context `AbortSignal` and discard stale
  network work when it aborts.
- Press `Ctrl+K`/`Cmd+K` or call `controller.openCommandPalette()` for global
  editor commands. Configure `commandPaletteItems`; do not create document-wide
  key listeners in application code.
- Listen to `commandExecuted` and `mentionSelected` only for user-action side
  effects. The canonical model still changes through normal editor transactions.
- Use `neuralEditorSlashMenu`, `neuralEditorMentionMenu`, and
  `neuralEditorCommandPalette` for custom rendering. Use the supplied signals,
  selection callbacks, and close callbacks. Do not access Tiptap plugin state or
  manually mount/reposition overlays.
- Suggestion and context overlays are mutually coordinated. Keep
  `menuAppendTo="body"` unless a deliberate editor-local stacking context is
  required.
- Slash commands and palette items execute local controller operations. They do
  not imply HTTP, AI, upload, or persistence behavior.

## AI request and review rules

- NeuralNg Editor does not call AI providers. Use `controller.requestAi()` and
  handle `(aiRequest)` in application code.
- Send the request's structured document, selection snapshot, stable node IDs,
  schema version, and base revision to the application-owned AI service. Do not
  scrape the `contenteditable` DOM and do not send generated HTML as the
  canonical source.
- AI services must return `NeuralEditorAiProposal` values containing only
  supported structured operations. Never return raw executable JavaScript,
  mutate the editor directly, or inject unsanitized HTML.
- Call `controller.previewAiProposal()` before applying a proposal. Preview uses
  ephemeral ProseMirror decorations and must not change `[(value)]`.
- Apply changes only after explicit user approval with
  `controller.acceptAiProposal()`. Reject with `rejectAiProposal()`; rejection
  removes decorations and leaves the canonical JSON unchanged.
- Respect `baseRevision`. Treat `aiOperationConflict` as a required rebase or
  fresh-request boundary. Never replace a stale proposal's revision with the
  current revision.
- A normal document edit invalidates the active preview. Do not keep stale
  visual suggestions visible after user edits.
- Use `(aiProposalPreviewed)`, `(aiProposalAccepted)`,
  `(aiProposalRejected)`, `(aiOperationConflict)`, and
  `(aiRequestCancelled)` for side effects and analytics.
- Customize the review UI with `ng-template[neuralEditorAiReview]`. Use the
  supplied callbacks and signals; do not mount another overlay, duplicate
  accept/reject state, or apply operations outside the controller.
- The default review UI follows `menuAppendTo`, supports mobile layout, and is
  part of the shared overlay coordination model.

## Conversion and persistence

- Use `editorDocumentFromHtml()` to import HTML and
  `editorDocumentToHtml()`/`editorDocumentToText()` for derived output.
- The default serializers understand the current Beta schema, including images and mentions. Pass the
  exact custom extension set when the document contains additional nodes or
  marks.
- Save documents in application code and persist a schema version beside
  long-lived JSON.
- Editor does not save data, upload files, call AI models, open collaboration
  connections, or perform backend sanitization.

## Security

- JSON is not a security boundary. Validate document structure, links, colors,
  table attributes, pasted content, and custom node attributes on the server.
- Sanitize generated HTML for its final destination.
- Never treat client-side toolbar palettes or schema checks as authorization or
  backend validation.

## Integration

- `extensions` are initialization-time in the alpha API and append to the
  defaults with top-level last-write-wins behavior.
- To replace StarterKit or the default schema, disable
  `includeDefaultExtensions` and provide every required extension.
- `readonly` keeps content readable and selectable while blocking edits.
  `disabled` also removes the editor from normal keyboard interaction.
- Use `unstyled` or global unstyled mode for headless rendering. Structural
  classes and ARIA relationships remain.

## Collaboration, comments, tracked changes, and snapshots

Use `NeuralEditorCollaborationConfig` with an application-owned `Y.Doc`.
NeuralNg does not create a collaboration backend, room, token, or provider.
The optional provider must expose the small structural provider contract.

When collaboration is enabled, the Yjs document is the live source of truth.
Do not initialize the editor with remote content before the provider has synced.
Do not bind autosave logic to every remote update without throttling and origin
checks. Collaboration disables StarterKit history and uses Yjs collaboration
undo/redo.
Treat `collaboration.document`, `provider`, `field`, and `fragment` as
initialization-only. Recreate the Editor when the room or field changes.

Pass `collaborationUser` with stable `id`, `name`, and `color` values. Presence
comes from provider awareness and is ephemeral. Never persist awareness state as
canonical editor content.

Use `enableComments` for inline plain-text comment threads. Thread data is stored
in the configured Yjs comments map when collaboration is active. Authentication,
permissions, notifications, moderation, and server persistence belong to the
application.

Use `trackedChangesMode="suggesting"` to record local text insertions and
deletions as review marks. Remote collaboration transactions are deliberately
ignored. Alpha 4 tracked changes are not an audit log and do not cover every
possible structural or formatting edit.

Use `[(snapshots)]` for portable JSON checkpoints. Snapshot creation does not
upload or persist anything. Save snapshots in application code. For exact CRDT
history or compliance-grade versioning, use a backend/provider history system.

Never combine independent Yjs documents for the same room. Never seed content on
an unsynchronized collaborative document. Do not mutate `Y.Doc` content and the
Editor `value` independently.
